memory_annotations.evidence_summary: No recurring travel preference was established. Marcus selected the Tuesday arrival for this Richmond trip because it protects a specific Wednesday meeting, while retaining the Wednesday itinerary as a cost comparison.

messages.content: Let’s settle the Richmond flights before looking at hotels. Compare the Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning options against the meeting and walkthrough, then pick the practical itinerary. Don’t buy anything.

I have two nonstop outbound choices from ORD to RIC: Tuesday, August 12, from 6:05 p.m. to 9:12 p.m., or Wednesday, August 13, from 7:10 a.m. to 10:18 a.m. Your regional meeting starts Wednesday at 1:30 p.m. downtown, and the restaurant walkthrough is Thursday from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. Is the meeting venue still near East Main Street?
Yes, two blocks from Main Street Station. How much time does the Wednesday flight really leave me?

RIC to that part of downtown is normally about 20-25 minutes by car, but I would allow 35-45 minutes around midday, plus 20-30 minutes to get off the plane and reach the pickup area. If the flight lands on time at 10:18, you would likely reach the meeting area around 11:15. That leaves roughly two hours. A delay of an hour would reduce the margin to about one hour; a delay approaching two hours would put the meeting at risk.
And the Tuesday flight means I’m paying for two hotel nights instead of one.

Correct. Tuesday arrival requires lodging Tuesday and Wednesday nights. The Wednesday morning flight requires only Wednesday night. The Tuesday outbound is $268 and the Wednesday outbound is $203. Paired with the later Thursday nonstop return at $218, airfare totals are $486 for Tuesday travel and $421 for Wednesday travel, before the hotel difference.
Remind me why the earlier Thursday return doesn’t work.

The early return leaves RIC at 12:20 p.m. With the walkthrough ending at 11:00, you would need to leave almost immediately and would have little margin for discussion, traffic, or security. The later nonstop leaves at 6:35 p.m. and arrives at ORD at 7:52 p.m., so it preserves the full walkthrough and gets you home around bedtime.
Is there anything between those two returns?

There is a 3:05 p.m. option connecting in Charlotte and arriving at ORD at 7:18 p.m. It costs $247 one way and adds connection risk while saving only 34 minutes versus the 6:35 nonstop arrival. The 6:35 p.m. nonstop remains the cleaner choice at $218.
So the real decision is $65 more in airfare plus another hotel night to remove most of the Wednesday risk.

Yes. The Tuesday itinerary costs $65 more in airfare, and its complete-trip premium will be $65 plus the Tuesday hotel night and associated taxes. In return, you arrive the night before and avoid tying the 1:30 meeting to the performance of a same-day flight.

Use Tuesday evening outbound and the 6:35 Thursday nonstop back. I don’t want a routine delay turning into a missed regional meeting. Carry both airfare totals into the hotel pricing so I can see the exact premium.

Selected for hotel pricing, without purchase: Tuesday, August 12, ORD 6:05 p.m.-RIC 9:12 p.m.; Wednesday regional meeting at 1:30 p.m. near Main Street Station; Thursday walkthrough from 9:00-11:00 a.m.; and Thursday, August 14, RIC 6:35 p.m.-ORD 7:52 p.m. Selected airfare is $486 round trip. I’ll price two hotel nights for Tuesday and Wednesday. For comparison, the Wednesday 7:10-10:18 a.m. outbound with the same return totals $421 and needs one hotel night, so the final comparison will show the full cost of the safer arrival. Nothing has been booked.
